overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by untimely approving 12 of 15 sets of minutes; three were not yet untimely, the attendance-based approval argument failed, and the broad minutes-completeness claim was declined.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve minutes of 15 meetings held between December 2021 and July 2022.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve 12 of the sets of meeting minutes at issue

allegations.summary: Minutes of the July 6, July 11, and July 20, 2022 meetings were alleged to be untimely when the complaint was filed.
allegations.key_passage: We note, however, that the minutes of the Board’s July 6, 11, and 20 meetings were not untimely as of when the complaint was filed with the Board on July 26

allegations.summary: Town said minutes of two meetings could not be approved because only one attending member remains on the Board, so they were posted but not approved.
allegations.key_passage: There is no requirement in the Open Meeting Law that only public body members in attendance at the meeting at issue vote to approve the minutes, nor does a lack of quorum of public body members who were in attendance during prior meetings constitute good cause for delay in approving minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint asked that Board minutes be comprehensive and summarize discussions on each subject, without identifying any specific deficient minutes.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint does not allege that any particular meeting minutes are insufficient, nor does the complaint identify what specifically may be missing from any particular meeting minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Approve the minutes of the December 6, 2021, and February 22, 2022, meetings within 30 days of the letter, if not already done.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that a finding of a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law. We also order the Board or a designee to approve the minutes of the December 6, 2021, and February 22, 2022, meetings within 30 days of the date of this letter, if it has not yet done so.
